correctness.rationale: For a nontrivial word split uv the rotation vu ends in u, so a non-overlapping code contains at most one word from each rotation class, and a nonprimitive word is excluded by its self-border. For weight three, a nonprimitive word must be a triple repeat of a block with one 1, possible only at 3|n, with exactly n/3 labeled words. Division by n after excluding these gives floor((n−1)(n−2)/6). For t=floor(n/3), the construction uses gaps (a,b,c) in 0^a1 0^b1 0^c1 with a≥t>c. A matching one-1 prefix and suffix would require a≤C, impossible; a matching two-1 pair requires b=C and a≤B for suffix-word gaps (A,B,C). Equal total lengths then give c=A+B−a≥A≥t, also impossible. Other proper prefix lengths cannot match a suffix (all suffixes end in 1, and the third 1 ends the word). Independently, every primitive cyclic gap triple has both a gap ≥t and a gap <t: all gaps ≥t would sum too high, and all gaps <t sum to at most 3t−3, with equality only at the excluded periodic triple. There is exactly one low-to-high transition in a mixed cyclic triple, so the construction selects exactly one representative. This proves all lengths including n=4 and multiples of three. At n=6,9,12,15,18 it found 2,3,4,5,6 nonprimitive words and code sizes 3,9,18,30,45. These are bounded checks only. Scope is linear binary words of the same length n≥4, exactly three ones, with self-pairs included.

evidence: For gcd(n,3)=1, put height increments +3 on zeros and −(n−3) on ones. There is a unique rotation with all proper prefix heights positive, and suffix heights are negative. Positivity for the first two 1-terminated prefixes is exactly a≥t and c<t. Thus the coprime construction follows from the usual unique-minimum cyclic positive-excursion argument.

value.rationale: The known rotation obstruction is only an upper bound until one can choose compatible linear representatives across classes. This explicit construction shows saturation even when the coprime excursion method fails to cover all classes, giving a complete answer in the first sparse three-gap regime with a possible equal-height return. That is a useful structural extremal fact beyond a small table or the routine necklace count; it is not a claim about weight four or greater.
